#4410. For decades, we were told to avoid full-fat dairy. New research says otherwise

For years, people have been encouraged to choose low-fat or fat-free dairy products to protect their hearts and manage their weight. But growing scientific evidence suggests that full-fat dairy may not carry the health risks many have come to expect.

A new Canadian study led by University of Toronto professor Harvey Anderson adds to that evidence. Researchers found that adults who consumed three servings of full-fat dairy each day for 12 weeks did not experience harmful changes in body weight, body composition, energy metabolism, or blood cholesterol levels compared with participants following a diet containing little dairy.

Even more surprisingly, participants who consumed more dairy showed improvements in blood pressure and obtained greater amounts of several important nutrients.

The findings, published in The Journal of Nutrition, raise new questions about longstanding dietary recommendations and suggest that the health effects of dairy may be more complicated than its saturated fat content alone would indicate.

For decades, nutrition guidelines in Canada and many other countries have recommended choosing low-fat or fat-free milk, yogurt, and other dairy products. The main concern has been saturated fat, which can raise levels of LDL cholesterol in the blood.

Often called "bad" cholesterol, LDL can contribute to fatty deposits in the arteries. Over time, this buildup can increase the risk of heart attacks, strokes, and other cardiovascular problems.

Because full-fat dairy contains more saturated fat than reduced-fat alternatives, health authorities have traditionally encouraged people to limit their intake.

However, research examining what happens when people actually consume full-fat dairy has produced a more complicated picture.

Anderson, a professor of nutritional sciences at the University of Toronto's Temerty Faculty of Medicine, points out that numerous studies involving humans have failed to find a clear association between full-fat dairy consumption and poor health outcomes.

Other research has even identified potential protective effects. That includes a recent study led by Temerty Medicine professor Kozeta Milliku, which found an association between whole-fat milk consumption and a lower risk of childhood obesity.

These findings have prompted scientists to investigate whether dairy foods behave differently in the body than their individual nutrients might suggest.

What Happened When Adults Ate Full-Fat Dairy Every Day?

To explore the question, Anderson and his colleagues conducted a 12-week study involving 74 adults with overweight or obesity.

Participants were randomly assigned to one of three dietary approaches. The first group followed a calorie-restricted diet containing little dairy. The second consumed three daily servings of dairy while maintaining an energy-neutral diet, meaning their calorie intake was intended to match the energy their bodies used. The third also consumed three servings of dairy each day but otherwise ate without specific calorie restrictions.

All participants received guidance based on Canada's food guide, and the researchers supplied full-fat dairy products during the study.

At the end of 12 weeks, the team compared several measures of metabolic health, including body weight, body composition, and cholesterol levels.

The results challenged expectations. Participants who consumed three servings of dairy daily did not show meaningful differences in weight gain, body composition, or blood cholesterol compared with those who ate little dairy.

The higher-dairy groups also experienced improvements in blood pressure and consumed more calcium, protein, and vitamin D. These nutrients play essential roles in maintaining healthy bones, supporting muscle function, and regulating numerous processes throughout the body.

"Those that had three servings of dairy didn't have adverse levels of blood cholesterol or lipids or evidence of insulin resistance," says Anderson.

Blood lipids are fats and fat-like substances circulating in the bloodstream, including cholesterol and triglycerides. Insulin resistance occurs when the body's cells become less responsive to insulin, making it harder to regulate blood sugar and increasing the risk of type 2 diabetes.

Although the results are encouraging, the study was relatively small and lasted only three months. Longer and larger studies are needed to determine whether the findings translate into lasting health benefits or changes in cardiovascular disease risk.

Why might full-fat dairy have different health effects than researchers would predict from its saturated fat content?

One possible explanation is the dairy matrix hypothesis, an idea that emphasizes how the physical structure of food influences the way the body processes its nutrients.

Rather than treating milk, cheese, or yogurt as simple collections of fat, protein, vitamins, and minerals, this theory considers how those components interact within the food itself.

"With dairy products, it's got two proteins -- casein and whey -- that are bound together with fat and with nutrients mixed in," says Anderson.

Casein and whey are the two major types of protein found in milk. Both provide amino acids that the body uses to build and maintain tissues, but they are digested and absorbed at different rates.

According to Anderson, the complex arrangement of proteins, fats, and other nutrients in dairy products can help regulate how quickly those nutrients are released during digestion.

This means the body's response to eating a whole dairy food may differ from its response to consuming an equivalent amount of saturated fat on its own.

The broader implication is that a food's health effects cannot always be predicted by examining a single ingredient. Its structure, nutritional composition, and interactions among nutrients may all matter.

Why the Findings Could Be Important for Older Adults

The researchers believe these results could be particularly relevant for older people, who often need to obtain sufficient protein and essential nutrients while consuming fewer calories.

As people age, their overall energy requirements frequently decrease. However, maintaining muscle mass, bone strength, and other important bodily functions still requires adequate nutrition.

That can make it difficult to meet nutritional needs, particularly for people with smaller appetites.

Anderson explains that dairy products offer a familiar, convenient source of concentrated nutrition. They provide protein, calcium, and other nutrients in foods that many older adults already enjoy and regularly consume.

The new findings suggest that including full-fat dairy in a balanced diet may help people meet these nutritional requirements without necessarily worsening cholesterol levels or markers associated with diabetes risk.

However, the study did not directly establish whether long-term consumption prevents or increases diabetes, heart disease, or other chronic conditions.

Rethinking Nutrition Advice Beyond Individual Nutrients

Beyond the debate over dairy fat, the research highlights a broader challenge in nutrition science: judging the health effects of entire foods rather than focusing exclusively on individual nutrients.

Traditional dietary advice has often emphasized reducing specific components, such as saturated fat. Although these recommendations are grounded in evidence about cardiovascular risk, researchers increasingly recognize that different foods containing the same nutrients may not have identical effects on health.

The University of Toronto findings contribute to this discussion by showing that full-fat dairy can be incorporated into certain diets without the unfavorable short-term metabolic changes that might be expected from its saturated fat content.

That does not mean saturated fat is harmless or that everyone should switch to full-fat dairy. Instead, it suggests that the overall food, its nutritional structure, and the broader dietary pattern deserve consideration.

For people trying to navigate changing nutrition recommendations and conflicting health messages, Anderson favors a practical approach rather than complicated dietary rules.

"Keep it simple, eat a variety of foods and not too much of anything."

This research was supported by Dairy Research Cluster 3 under the Canadian Agricultural Partnership AgriScience Program, and the Mitacs Accelerate program.

#4407. Major trial challenges how doctors decide who really needs statins

A major clinical trial has raised new questions about how doctors decide who should take statins to prevent heart attacks and strokes. Researchers found that using heart scans to guide treatment decisions produced the same observed rate of major cardiovascular events as traditional risk assessments, even though the scans led to far fewer recommendations to begin taking statins.

The findings, presented during a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026, also revealed a striking difference in how consistently patients took their medication. Those advised to use statins based on calcium buildup in their coronary arteries were substantially more likely to follow their treatment recommendations.

Although the results suggest that heart scans could help doctors make more targeted treatment decisions, the trial did not establish that the scan approach was as effective as conventional risk assessment. Researchers say additional studies are needed to determine whether it offers a better strategy for preventing cardiovascular disease.

Why Predicting Heart Disease Risk Remains a Challenge

Cardiovascular disease remains the world's leading cause of illness and death. Much of this burden comes from atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), which develops when fatty deposits known as plaque accumulate inside arteries, restricting blood flow and increasing the risk of heart attacks and strokes. Coronary artery disease and ischemic stroke are two major forms of this condition.

Several common factors increase the likelihood of developing ASCVD, including smoking, diabetes, high blood pressure, and elevated cholesterol. Doctors use these factors to estimate a person's cardiovascular risk and determine whether preventive medications are appropriate.

Statins are among the most widely used treatments for lowering that risk. These medications reduce cholesterol levels, particularly low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, often called LDL or bad cholesterol. They also help lower the likelihood of serious cardiovascular complications.

However, identifying which patients stand to benefit from statins remains a significant challenge. Some people who eventually experience a heart attack do not appear to be at particularly high risk under conventional screening methods.

"For far too many patients, the first symptom of ASCVD is a heart attack," said Doctor Joseph B Muhlestein from the Intermountain Medical Center, Murray, USA, the Principal Investigator of the CorCal Outcomes trial. "Statins have been shown to be highly effective in the prevention of ASCVD; however, there is a major gap in risk assessment, statin initiation, and statin persistence."

According to Muhlestein, many people who suffer their first heart attack, particularly younger adults, would not previously have been classified as having enough cardiovascular risk to justify statin treatment. This limitation has prompted researchers to investigate whether directly examining the arteries might provide more useful information.

Can Heart Calcium Scans Improve Statin Decisions?

The CorCal Outcomes trial investigated two different approaches for determining which patients should be advised to begin statin therapy before experiencing a cardiovascular event.

The first relied on the pooled cohort equations (PCE), a commonly used risk assessment tool that estimates cardiovascular risk using traditional factors such as age, cholesterol levels, blood pressure, and smoking status.

The second approach measured coronary artery calcium (CAC), which provides a more direct indication of plaque buildup in the arteries supplying the heart.

This measurement uses a computed tomography (CT) scan to detect calcium deposits in the coronary arteries. Calcium can accumulate within atherosclerotic plaque, making it a useful marker of underlying coronary artery disease, even in people who have not developed symptoms.

Unlike traditional risk calculators, which estimate the likelihood of future cardiovascular problems based on personal characteristics and health measurements, calcium scans provide evidence of disease already present in the coronary arteries.

Researchers wanted to determine whether using this information to guide statin recommendations could improve cardiovascular outcomes.

Nearly 5,800 Patients Put Both Methods to the Test

The trial enrolled 5,772 patients from the Canyons and Desert regions of Intermountain Health Care in the United States. Participants had no known history of ASCVD or diabetes and had not previously received statin therapy.

Their average age was 64, and women accounted for 51% of the study population.

Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to one of two groups. One group received statin treatment guidance based on traditional cardiovascular risk scores, while the other received recommendations based on coronary calcium scan results.

Both patients and their physicians were informed of the treatment recommendations generated by the study protocol. However, the final decision about whether to start taking statins remained with the patients and their doctors.

The researchers then tracked major cardiovascular events (MACE; all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and arterial revascularization).

This combined outcome included death from any cause, heart attacks, strokes, and procedures to restore blood flow through narrowed or blocked arteries.

Heart Scans Led to Far Fewer Statin Recommendations

After an average follow-up of 4.2 years, researchers found that major cardiovascular events occurred at exactly the same observed rate in both groups.

A total of 2.7% of patients in each group experienced one of the events included in the study's primary outcome. The estimated relative risk over time was also nearly identical (hazard ratio 0.99; 95% confidence interval 0.71 to 1.38; p=0.045 for noninferiority).

However, this similarity did not establish that the two strategies were equally effective. The study failed to meet its predetermined statistical requirement for demonstrating that the calcium scan approach was not meaningfully worse than conventional risk assessment.

A notable difference emerged in how frequently patients were advised to begin taking statins.

Participants evaluated using traditional risk scores received recommendations to start statin therapy more than three times as often as those whose decisions were guided by coronary calcium measurements.

Despite this substantial difference in treatment recommendations, both groups experienced the same observed rate of major cardiovascular events during the follow-up period.

A Surprising Difference in Statin Adherence

Perhaps the most intriguing finding involved whether patients actually followed their prescribed treatment.

Among those advised to take statins, patients whose recommendations were based on calcium scans were much more likely to adhere to their medication regimen than those assessed using traditional cardiovascular risk factors.

The difference was substantial (62% vs. 23%).

In other words, patients recommended statins based on visible evidence of calcium buildup in their arteries were approximately 2.7 times as likely to follow their medication regimen.

One possible explanation is that seeing evidence of disease in their own arteries makes patients more motivated to take preventive medication. However, the trial did not establish why adherence differed so dramatically between the groups.

The findings raise the possibility that coronary calcium scans could influence not only which patients receive statin recommendations, but also whether those patients consistently take the medications.

What the Findings Mean for Heart Disease Prevention

Despite these potentially important differences, the researchers emphasized that the study could not establish whether calcium scan-guided treatment provides cardiovascular protection comparable to traditional risk assessment.

One important limitation was that fewer participants experienced major cardiovascular events than the investigators had anticipated. With fewer events to analyze, the trial had less statistical power to determine whether a meaningful difference existed between the two approaches.

"The power of the study to detect a difference was reduced by the lower-than-expected event rates and we did not demonstrate noninferiority between the groups," said Doctor Muhlestein, who concluded: "The study did provide important hypothesis-generating insights into the efficiency of statin initiation and adherence when decisions are based on CAC scoring. Taken together, our data could be used to plan an additional well-powered randomized trial comparing CAC with current risk factor-based algorithms."

The findings may help researchers design future trials capable of determining whether coronary calcium scans can improve the efficiency of statin prescribing without compromising cardiovascular protection.

Current European recommendations already recognize a potential role for these measurements. The 2025 Focused Update of the 2019 ESC/EAS Guidelines for the management of dyslipidemias recommends considering increased coronary calcium scores, when available, as an additional factor in cardiovascular risk assessment.

This guidance applies particularly to people at moderate cardiovascular risk or those whose estimated risk falls near the threshold at which preventive medication would normally be recommended.

For these individuals, evidence of calcium buildup may help doctors make more informed decisions when the need for statin therapy is uncertain.

The CorCal Outcomes findings add to the discussion by suggesting that heart scans may also influence how faithfully patients follow treatment. Whether that advantage translates into better long-term cardiovascular outcomes remains an important question for future research.

Materials provided by European Society of Cardiology. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4406. The Roottrees are Dead has you investigating a complex family tree with 90s technology

Mystery games tend to fall into very familiar divisions, with point-and-click adventures or hidden-object puzzlers as you attempt to unpack a mystery, such as a murder or disappearance. But The Roottrees are Dead offers a very different take on the format as it launches for iOS and Android, complete with an extra mystery!

The Roottrees are Dead sees the story kick off with the deaths of the titular wealthy family, and your introduction in the role of investigator. Your job is not to figure out what killed them; that's already clear, but instead you have to track down their various relatives who, thanks to the wishes of an eccentric patriarch, are now entitled to a share of the enormous Roottree fortune.

Dead and buried To accomplish this, you'll be given the most high-tech tools... of the late 1990s. That means browsing the early internet, examining photos and making connections between family members in familiar red string patterns.

The Roottrees are Dead takes you back to a time just before the explosion of the internet, and the rise of digital archiving as we now know it. And that makes for a surprisingly engrossing take on a mystery game as you unpick details, make connections and rely on your own intuition.

The mobile release also comes packaged with a bonus mystery, Roottreemania, offering even more content for you to sink your teeth into! And with a sterling critical reception, it might well be time for the true crime and mystery fans amongst you to give The Roottrees Are Dead a go on iOS and Android!

In the meantime, if low-res is your kind of thing, then you might find another recent release quite interesting. Titanium Court is a match-three/RTS hybrid, and one that really experiments with everything from gameplay to UI. Check out my Titanium Court review to find out whether it holds up!

#4405. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

#4404. PHYSINT Star Bill Skarsgård has Become ‘Enamored’ with Hideo Kojima and His Works

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

If a single person could be considered to be the definitive face of auteur game development, it would be Hideo Kojima, hands down. The man was already showing his chops in putting together unforgettable productions back in the Metal Gear Solid days, and ever since going into business for himself with Kojima Productions, his worlds and stories have only gotten bigger and bolder.

All of those qualities alone more than qualify Kojima for auteur status, but there’s also a little bit more to it than that. Kojima possesses, for lack of a better term, a certain magnetism, both in his person and his production, that inexplicably draws powerful, prominent individuals from across the entertainment spectrum. You just have to look at the original Death Stranding and its star-studded cast to see the kind of magnetic pull a Kojima trip possesses.

Very little is currently known about PHYSINT, one of Kojima’s next big-budget productions that was rescued from the brink by XBOX when Sony bailed out over the summer, but apparently, its star, Bill Skarsgård, was already well aboard Mister Kojima’s wild ride well before he signed on. He spoke to this during a recent appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, as well as the inherent power that comes with Kojima’s works.

Joining an already stacked cast for PHYSINT, which features Charlee Fraser, Don Lee, and Minami Hamabe, is none other than Bill Skarsgård.

As Skarsgård explained, he grew up playing Kojima’s games during his time at Konami, chief among them the Metal Gear series. By his own admission, Skarsgård has played every single Metal Gear game that is commercially available, finding himself repeatedly drawn into the elaborate, intricate world that Kojima was piecing together story-by-story.

Skarsgård has played every single Metal Gear game that is commercially available.

As Skarsgård became more interested in Kojima’s creations, he became more interested in Kojima himself. “I was very enamoured by him and the sort of the mythology or the universes that he creates, but also the sort of mystique and allure about him as well,” he explained.

Hideo Kojima shared several new details about PHYSINT, and it looks like the legendary developer is going back to full stealth.

Later in the interview, as Skarsgård described the process of motion capture that was going into PHYSINT’s development, he marveled at how the planned game will feature both eight hours of narrative alongside an entire, living world populated by photorealistic people and settings.

“I think he's a pioneer, and keeps going out to untrodden waters,” he said of Kojima.

Skarsgård briefly recalled a discussion he had about filmmaking with Kojima during PHYSINT’s motion capture process. It’s no secret that, in addition to video games, Kojima is well-versed in the cinematic arts, both on a technical level and just as a good old fashioned lover of movies, as you can tell from the many film references and direct shout-outs that pepper his games.

Interestingly, though, when Skarsgård asked Kojima if he ever wanted to make an actual movie someday rather than a game, Kojima said no, because he wants to make something with the cinematic potential of traditional film combined with the inherent interactivity of a video game, and a regular film can’t do that. “At this point, what he's doing is inventing a new medium,” Skarsgård said.

All we currently know about PHYSINT, aside from its major stars in Bill Skarsgård, Charlee Fraser, Ma Dong-seok, and Minami Hamabe, is that it’s apparently going to be an action-espionage game in a similar vein to the Metal Gear series. The promotional tagline on its initial reveal poster is “The Next Cold War Begins.” Based on Skarsgård’s gushing, though, it’s going to be quite the ambitious multimedia project, the kind of elaborate, once-per-generation creation that only an auteur like Kojima could bring to life. So, y’know, business as usual.

New PHYSINT exhibition displays feature Metal Gear-like mechs, offering an intriguing glimpse of Kojima's next spy-action game.

Of all the upcoming releases we've covered, one that's kept my curiosity is UnGodly, the upcoming hack 'n slash RPG from Azra Games and Mark Otero, one of the key figures behind Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes. And in its most recent gameplay trailer, we not only got the announcement that it would be coming to iPhone Duo, but also a good look at its gameplay!

It's easy to see why UnGodly is so consistently described as Frazetta-inspired, because everyone lacks a shirt, or at the very least seems to lack the buttons for them. #4401. The MongolZ end FURIA’s winning run as NAVI send Falcons out of IEM Beijing

The MongolZ beat world No.1 FURIA to reach the IEM Beijing semi-finals, while NAVI eliminated big-spending Falcons in the group stage. The results reshape the picture of the main contenders before the PGL Major Singapore opens on 24 November.

Against world No.1 FURIA on Wednesday, The MongolZ recovered after dropping the opening map. MOUZ have also booked a semi-final place after going unbeaten in Group B.

The defeat ended a seven-game winning run for FURIA, HLTV said, although the match was not an elimination game. FURIA had not lost since winning PGL Masters Bucharest. They now face BetBoom in the quarter-finals.

The second map, Cache, was FURIA’s own pick, and The MongolZ had lost on that map in each of their previous four attempts. This time they won it, then closed out the series on the third map.

The timing gives the result extra weight. IEM Beijing is ESL’s top-tier CS2 event and the last big tournament before the Major. FURIA are still alive, but the series shows they can be beaten by the sides around them.

Falcons went out in the Group A lower-bracket final. NAVI recovered from a narrow loss on the opening map and dominated the rest of the series. On the Mirage decider, NAVI won all 12 rounds of their T-side half.

w0nderful went 25-4 on Inferno. b1t then took over on Mirage.

For a big-spending organisation, an exit before the playoffs is a setback. Falcons share seventh to eighth place with Team Liquid, and the two teams earn the same amount. That compares with $360,000 for the champions.

Liquid also fell at the final hurdle. BetBoom beat them 2-1 to take the last playoff place in Group B. A zorte ace in round 23 of the Mirage decider swung the series. PARIVISION, who finished behind MOUZ in Group B, meet NAVI in the other quarter-final.

The $1,250,000 prize pool is split into $300,000 in player prize money and $950,000 in club share. The event is being played at the Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena in Beijing. It is listed as an ESL Pro Tour Masters event.

The playoffs are single-elimination best-of-three series. A best-of-three third-place match will also be played, and the grand final is best-of-five.

🏟️ Bloomage Biotech·Biohyalux ECM Arena pic.twitter.com/pr3rqLDijc

— ESL Counter-Strike (@ESLCS) November 4, 2026

Both quarter-finals take place on Friday 6 November, at 14:30 and 17:45 local time. The semi-finals follow on Saturday 7 November. The grand final is on Sunday 8 November.

Attention then turns to the PGL Major Singapore, the second CS2 Major of 2026. Its last four days will be played at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, which holds more than 12,000 spectators.

What are the Pocket Gamer team playing this weekend?

Happy Friday and welcome back to The Wrapp. With the weekend looming, it's time to think about what we'll all be playing over the next couple of days. Shaun and Iwan are eyeing some anime goodness, while Dann plans to investigate murder. Elsewhere, Catherine is winding down from a busy work trip by beating people up.

One thing I am hoping to do this weekend is acquire The Roottrees Are Dead, which I only semi-recently completed the initial story of on PC. Roottreemania (the second mode) is a lot more intense, investigative and involved, so I think it’ll suit mobile down to the ground.

I think the big number I'm waiting to automatically download over WiFi only is Warhammer Survivors (obviously). Although I preregistered for Monster Hunter Outlanders, I have yet to challenge my device.

I'm keeping an eye on itchy fan dev Strimp's Kitchen as they continue work on Meta Knightmare Stellar Symphony. Still, got plenty of fish to catch in Kirby Soft & Wet.

I’ll probably be dipping back into Titanium Court over the weekend. My review is now live, so it’s no spoiler to say this is one game I found at once a little frustrating by how artsy it’s obviously trying to be, but still very engaging. In terms of both gameplay and all the actual artistic stuff, Titanium Court holds up very well, and I feel like I’m still only scratching the surface.

I’ve also been eyeing Bleach Mirrors High, because after covering Monster Hunter Outlanders extensively, that feels like the logical next step for a ‘big’ launch. As a child, I casually watched quite a bit of anime. Cardcaptors, Sailor Moon, Dragon Ball, Gundam; whatever was on TV. But the first series I got into was Bleach. An old friend introduced me, and I was hooked.

Recently, the TV series wrapped up with Thousand-Year Blood War; love me some Quincy. And yet, there is a little mobile game called Bleach Mirrors High that carries on the narrative. And better yet, you get to make your own protagonist. I am a sucker for having OCs in great series, so I'll be here nerding out in the corner this weekend, trying to turn my phone into my Zanpakuto.

By the weekend, I’ll have just gotten back from a big work trip, and will likely have all my stuff (and my mind) scattered every which way. I suppose I need a calm puzzler of sorts to get my affairs in order, but to be honest, it’s Absolum that’s gotten my attention this week, so I’ll be hacking and slashing away at that. Unpacking my stuff will just have to wait!

While we have plenty of cool stuff on the horizon that appeals to me (Hello, Silver Palace and Gunboat God), nothing recently released is calling out to me. Having just finished and enjoyed Mafia: The Old Country, I'm drawn to something focused on telling a good story. Perhaps I'll peruse our list of the best narrative adventure games and see what appeals.

#4399. The Duskbloods Delayed To 2027 So FromSoftware Can Adjust 'Game Rules And Balancing'

While the 2025 reveal of the Switch 2 came with many surprises, none were as unexpected as The Duskbloods. It's a Switch 2 exclusive, multiplayer-only title from FromSoftware, the developer behind games like Dark Souls and Elden Ring; in other words, not your typical Nintendo game. While The Duskbloods was originally scheduled to launch sometime this year, today the developer announced it's pushing the game's launch to 2027.

According to a post on The Duskbloods' X account, the main reason for the delay was balance-related. Here's the full statement:

While development of "The Duskbloods" is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027. We apologize to players who have been kindly awaiting the release of this title and thank you for your patience and support. During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression. To further enhance these aspects, we have decided to move the launch, allowing time for final adjustments to game rules and balancing.

We attended a hands-on preview session earlier this year and came away very positive, and sentiment was similar following the game's closed network test (that is, when the servers were working properly). It's not surprising that the devs have changes in mind following so much public feedback, though it is a little surprising that it will take until sometime next year for those adjustments to be complete.

To tide you over until the game's launch, check out our in-depth preview impressions or watch the video above to hear our live commentary over gameplay footage. You can also hear us discuss the game on our podcast, The Game Informer Show.

#4397. Assassin’s Creed Franchise Update Reveals Codename Hexe News Coming Next Year, New Game Plus for Valhalla, And Confirms No New Remakes

Ubisoft has released a fall update on the Assassin’s Creed franchise, providing news big and small on its flagship series. The news includes updates for existing games and smaller but significant insights on the various upcoming Assassin’s Creed games previously announced.

In terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new update coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:

This news comes a few days after New Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

Codname Invictis, a PvP multiplayer game, remains in development as Ubisoft shares it has incorporated feedback from players who, according to Ubisoft, “saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed.” To this end, Ubisoft has spent months reworking Invictis to reflect this vague feedback and say the game is “now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions.”

As for the next single-player Assassin’s Creed, Codename Hexe, Ubisoft says it will share the next major update on this game in 2027. First announced in 2022, Codename Hexe is set during the 17th-century reign of the Holy Roman Empire, and the era's witch hunts will play a significant role.

With the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this year, Ubisoft has given fans what they'll likely see as a disappointing update on potential future remakes: “One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development. Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories.”

However, Ubisoft adds that this door isn’t closed for good. “Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back,” says Ubisoft.

Ubisoft’s next update concerns the live-action Assassin's Creed series in production for Netflix. They say the show is “nearing completion” in Rome and that award-winning composer Hannah Peel (Insomnia, Rogue Agent, Game of Thrones: The Last Watch) is composing the score.

Lastly, Ubisoft teases big celebrations are planned for 2027, which marks the 20th anniversary of the Assassin's Creed franchise. It's keeping details to itself for now, but states it's "preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments. "

For more on Assassin's Creed, check out our review of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

#4395. What To Do If The Unlearn Button Is Missing In WoW: Forever

World of Warcraft: Forever lets you learn up to two primary professions at a time, but you aren't stuck with your first choice. Maybe you picked Mining and Herbalism to earn gold selling materials at the auction house while leveling, only to decide later you'd rather craft your own gear or potions.

Fortunately, you can unlearn a profession to make room for a new one. Before switching, though, it's worth knowing where to find the option and what happens to your progress. We also encountered an issue with the unlearn button, but found a workaround that fixed it for us.

You don't need to visit a trainer to unlearn a profession.

Once you confirm, that profession is removed, and its slot becomes available. You can then visit a profession trainer to learn a new profession.

However, unlearning a profession resets your skill progress and removes the recipes you've unlocked. If you take up that profession again later, your previous progress won't return automatically, and you'll have to relearn its recipes. This applies to both purchased and looted recipes.

Only primary professions count toward the two-profession limit. Cooking, Fishing, and First Aid are secondary professions, and you can learn all three without using either primary slot.

A World of Warcraft Forever player has taken matters into their own hands after the flood of new Olympus guilds overseen by Asmongold.

We encountered an issue where the red X appeared as a blank space in the Professions window. The Unlearn tooltip appeared next to the blank space when we hovered over it, but we couldn't click the button. Changing the UI Scale in our game fixed the issue and let us unlearn professions again.

Unlearning a profession in World of Warcraft: Forever only takes a few steps, and adjusting the UI Scale may help if the red X isn't appearing. Just double-check your choice before confirming. You can always learn the profession again, but your previous skill progress and recipes won't automatically return.

#4394. Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek, X-Men, And Myriad Video Games Actor, Passes Away

According to a report from The Hollywood Reporter, actor Sir Patrick Stewart has passed away at the age of 86. Stewart spokesperson, Kelly Bush Novak, shared that he died after “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.”

Stewart was best known for his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation (and its various spinoffs) and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but he did plenty of video game performing, too. Stewart played Emperor Uriel Septim VII in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, one of the first characters you meet in the game, and Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. He also played Jean-Luc Picard in about 10 different Star Trek games and Charles Xavier in five different X-Men games.

Stewart will always be a crucial voice and face in the legacy of sci-fi entertainment. Jean-Luc Picard will undoubtedly be an enduring and important character in the Star Trek franchise, and that's thanks to Stewart's portrayal of the starship captain. His portrayal of Charles Xavier also helped to legitimize the comic book movie, and he will appear again as the character in this year's upcoming Avengers: Doomsday.

Our thoughts are with his friends and family, and the millions of fans (of which I include myself) who are mourning his loss. Let's all drink some Earl Grey tea in his honor today.

#4393. Switch 2 Surpasses 26 Million Units Sold, Hardware Sales Down By 37.4%

Nintendo has released its latest financial report, confirming that the Switch 2 has now sold over 26 million units since its launch last year.

Coming in at more accurate 26.35 million, unit sales for the first half of the current fiscal year totalled 6.49 million. This represents a year-on-year decrease of 37.4%, with the company shifting 10.36 million during the same period last year.

Don't fret, though! This is to be expected. Console sales for the Switch 2 were astronomical during its first year on sale, so a decrease during its second year isn't going to come as a surprise. Couple in the hardware price hikes earlier this year, and it's clear that momentum has taken an expected downward turn.

Still, 26 million though folks. 26. Million. It's creeping up on the N64's lifetime sales at 32.93 million.

Software performed much better. Nintendo shifted a total of 24.49 million Switch 2 games over the first half of the year, an uptick of 18.8% over the same period last year. Similarly, Switch 1 software sold 65.72 million, an increase of 6.8&%. Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream and Rhythm Heaven Groove helped Nintendo achieve this, selling 8.81 million and 2.89 million respectively.

Nintendo's forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 remains unchanged at this time, so it's currently expecting to sell a total of 16.5 million Switch 2 units during the period.

#4392. GTA 6 Could Get PC Release Soon to Avoid AI Clones, Says Former Rockstar Dev

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. Before joining the team at DualShockers, Lauren was a Features Writer at Adventure Gamers, a Guides Writer at Gameranx, as well as contributing as a News Writer at PCInvasion and Daily

The launch of GTA 6 is imminent, and thanks to Rockstar Games moving the pre-load date forward, the release of this highly anticipated game is starting to feel more real. However, not even the big dogs are safe from the likes of AI, as there are concerns Generative AI could be used by third parties to port the game on PC.

It’s becoming increasingly common to see an indie hit take off and AI-generated clones quickly following in an attempt to piggy back off of that success. One such example is the viral Needle In A Haystack game, which follows the premise of finding a needle hidden in over 10 million pieces of hay with your friends. Since then, various AI-generated rip offs began appearing on Steam, with one developer even stealing the original game’s code.

Rockstar's 38 new GTA 6 screenshots showcase incredibly detailed faces, Vice City's nightlife, and the gangs and scenes bringing Leonida to life.

Roblox is another platform that Needle In A Haystack, among other trending games, has popped up on. Since Roblox is free to play, anyone can play a near copy of a paid game, with a few microtransactions thrown in.

Although GTA 6 would be difficult to replicate in the same way, former Rockstar North technical director, Obbe Vermeij, believes AI is a threat to an official GTA 6 PC port, as discussed in an interview with Rock Paper Shotgun.

Vermeij acknowledges that Generative AI “really has changed the world," and believes, “I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking."

"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest, I don't see it," he says, but Take-Two Interactive aren’t completely powerless on the matter. “But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and maybe, like, you said, for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job.”

“But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years, how that's going to pan out."

It has been widely reported that GTA 6 will be released on PC during the first quarter of 2027. Neither Rockstar Games nor Take-Two has provided comment on the status of the arrival of GTA 6 on PC.

Not even the big dogs are safe from the likes of AI, as there are concerns Generative AI could be used by third parties to port the game on PC.

If GTA 6 does make its PC debut in the first quarter of 2027, it would land just a few months after its release on PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X|S platforms. Therefore, it would be a lot quicker than the PC release of GTA 5, which came out in April 2015, nearly two years after its roll out on console in September 2013.

Any AI-generated ports would likely face a DMCA takedown and will undoubtedly be nowhere near as polished or safe to run than the real deal.

As AI continues to advance, it will be interesting to see if it’s able to replicate a game as huge as GTA 6. The game is expected to require up to 212 GB of storage on console and is packed to the brim with approximately 80 hours of story content alone.

From DMA Design to GTA III, GTA V, and RDR2, let's take a look back at how Rockstar Games changed open-world gaming and why GTA 6 has so much to live up to.

#4391. Death Stranding Isolations Animated Series Gets New Teaser Trailer

A new teaser trailer for Death Stranding Isolations, an upcoming animated series coming exclusively to Disney+ and Hulu next year, premiered during Kojima Productions’ 10th Anniversary Exhibition Beyond the Strand. The series was first announced last year.

Death Stranding Isolations tells an original story in the Death Stranding universe set immediately after the events of the first game. Isolations is created by Japanese animation studio E&H Production (Ninja Kamui, Bullet/Bullet, Magic Knight Rayerath) and directed by Takayuki Sano.  Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima serves as executive producer.

Today’s teaser video provides the following story synopsis:

The Death Stranding—a catastrophic series of explosions caused when the dead crept into our world and collided with the living.

In the wake of this cataclysm, many were forced to live in absolute isolation—among them, a young girl. Although this lonely existence was forced upon her, she soon grows to prefer solitude, eschewing all opportunities for real human connection and allowing herself to be strung along by fate.

In Death Stranding, legendary game creator Hideo Kojima brought you a haunting vision of a shattered world. Now, that world expands into new frontiers with a brand-new animation series.

Under the guidance of director Takayuki Sano, world-class hand-drawn animations have been brought to life by renowned studio “E&H production” (NINJA KAMUI, BULLET/BULLET, the Magic Knight Rayearth television series).

The story is set in North America immediately after Sam—the protagonist of the game—reconnects the continent by means of the Chiral Network. However, as America is reborn from the ashes, the renewed connections that bind it together bring about new and unforeseen consequences.

In this tumultuous new landscape, there are some who walk a different path to the one chosen by Sam and his Bridges comrades: a wise old man who connects people through a method that defies all reckoning; a female soldier ensnared in a cycle of war and destruction; a boy who seethes with rage at the absurdity of his life...and of course, the girl who chose to sever all ties with the outside world...Fate has other plans for her, however, and chance encounters see her launched headfirst into a world she does not recognize.

Death Stranding Isolations is coming to Disney+ and Hulu in 2027. It’s one of the three planned big-screen adaptations of the series. An animated movie called Death Stranding: Mosquito (working title) is also in the works alongside a live-action Death Stranding film by A24.

For more on Death Stranding, check out our reviews for the first game and its 2025 sequel. You can also read the latest update on Kojima Productions’ upcoming stealth-espionage game, Physint.

#4390. EA Reportedly Closed BioWare To Invest In Developing Star Wars Battlefront III Instead Of The Next Mass Effect

Electronic Arts shut down the legendary RPG studio BioWare last week, ending development on an untitled fifth Mass Effect game. Since then, we've seen what appears to be a leaked trailer for the game, which suggests it might have been called Mass Effect Universe, and heard a sneak peek at what Grammy-winning composer Austin Wintory was cooking up for the beloved sci-fi RPG series. Over the past week, fans across the internet have tried to piece together how a publisher could decide to shut down a studio as prolific as BioWare, but according to a new Bloomberg report, the answer is Star Wars.

More specifically, Bloomberg writes that, presented with the opportunity to develop Star Wars Battlefront III with Disney, the publisher, which went private last year after a $55 billion acquisition,  chose to invest its money into that instead of BioWare's in-development Mass Effect sequel. The publication writes that EA looked at its portfolio for the coming years and had two massive sci-fi investments it could continue: Star Wars Battlefront III or BioWare's next Mass Effect. Even though Mass Effect was well into development, and even though the Battlefront threequel hasn't even entered development, EA chose to continue with the latter. And so BioWare was shut down, and Mass Effect development ended, though Bloomberg's sources say there are other, less significant reasons the studio was shuttered, too.

Those other factors include the poor reception to 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda, the failure of Anthem in 2019, and 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which, despite garnering positive critical reception, apparently missed EA's sales expectations by 50%.

There's also the uncomfortable reality that BioWare made progressive LGBTQIA+ positive games but was a studio within a publisher house now partially owned by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, a government fund from a country where same-sex activity, including marriage, is criminalized, sometimes punishable by death; these harsh laws extend to other facets of the LGBTQIA+ community. Another investment partner in this acquisition of EA is Affinity Partners, a Miami-based investment firm founded and run by former White House senior advisor Jared Kushner, who is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, a political figure who imposes laws that discriminate against the LGBTQIA+ community, especially the 1% of Americans who are transgender; Trump has also been known to mock this community in various ways. No official statements say BioWare shut down because of its progressive leanings, but one has to wonder if that was a factor, especially after reports that BioWare scrubbed diversity from demos to avoid negative feedback from EA (thanks, Kotaku).

When BioWare closed last week, only 50 employees remained, all working on the next Mass Effect, after years of layoffs at the studio.

A Mass Effect TV series is still in the works at Amazon, even though EA seems to have hung up Commander Shepard's video game suit for good.

#4389. Arc Raiders just keeps breaking its own Steam player records

Word of mouth has done wonders for the popularity of Arc Raiders, clearly more than all the pre-launch marketing and hype.

Arc Raiders just cannot be stopped. The extraction shooter from Embark Studios has once again attracted more players over the weekend than it has in its launch week, and over its first weekend on the market.

The positive reception the PvPvE game has garnered from players has clearly caused many of them to convince their friends to jump into this unique gem of a game.

The day Arc Raiders launched, it peaked at 264,673 concurrent players on Steam. Although not massive, it was quite a bit more than the game’s most popular - free - beta test managed to attract.

That figure was broken yet again over the game’s first weekend, with Arc Raiders having reached 354,836 concurrent players on Steam. This is where many thought it would settle, as we start to see the gradual - and expected - decline of player numbers.

To everyone’s surprise, however, Arc Raiders shattered even that record yet again on Sunday, November 9. According to SteamDB, the game peaked at 462,488 concurrent players on Steam, which is a sizeable increase on its launch day numbers. Indeed, should this trend continue, Arc Raiders is going to be well on its way to doubling its initial launch record.

While a few games have broken their launch Steam player records in the past, it’s incredibly rare to see it happen - especially twice in such a short period after launch. Embark clearly has a winner on its hands here.

Arc Raiders’ next big moment is the game’s first post-launch map, which is set to arrive at some point this month, alongside new Quests and other gameplay items. Seeing as how the Steam concurrent record has been broken twice, there’s every chance the arrival of the new map will bring another boost to player numbers.

If you’re among the millions of players who have been exploring the Rust Belt, you’re probably wondering where to find prickly pears, where to find lemons and apricots, and where to find olives - and those links will answer all of those questions. And, if you just jumped in over the weekend, you’re definitely going to find these Arc Raiders tips very helpful.

#4387. The Top 10 Best Horror Games To Play This Halloween

Humans are drawn to horror in all forms, real life and fiction. Perhaps it’s the desire to get as close to death as possible without actually dying; perhaps it’s the morality of life and knowing death comes for all of us; perhaps all our heads are just a little miswired. Whatever the reason, we flock to movies where supernatural entities and puppets on tricycles upend otherwise lovely lives, TV shows where murderous cults kill and stump local detectives, and books where the words on the page seem to follow you to bed. Games, however, go a step further, letting you enter the horror and control it (or become its victim), and you could argue that, as a result, they’re the most immersive form of fiction.

We at Game Informer love a healthy dose of horror from time to time, and we often review games like this. Some terrify us. Others… don’t. And the best ones stick with us for years and years after the credits. Below is a list of 10 of the best horror games we’ve played recently. This isn’t an all-time list, so don’t fret if your personal favorite isn’t here. Instead, this is a collection of 10 horror games ordered by release date that we think are great for spooky season and beyond. Let us know in the comments what you would add to the list!

The cozy corner of the horror genre seems to have exploded overnight, and now tons of new slice-of-life horror games are in various stages of development. That said, the team behind newcomer The Village in the Shade is no stranger to the form; they made the Yomawari series, a cute-and-terrifying collection of creepy virtual tales. The Village in the Shade takes things back to the homestead, giving you (a child who emerged from a hole in the ground and was immediately given the responsibility of running an entire farm by yourself) the freedom to plant, sow, reap, ranch, and more. Just follow the important rules: don't go out at night, don't share secrets, and don't leave the village among others. You wouldn't want to break the rules, right? You could, theoretically, go about your idyllic rural living. But as you unravel the threads of what this village is, who you are, and why you're here, it's hard not to get drawn into the strange, mysterious, delightfully disturbing truths hiding in its shadows. Just don't forget to water your turnips before you go sneaking out again.

Fans of survival horror and old-school FMV adventure games will find plenty to love (and fear) in Tenebris Somnia. When a young woman visits her ex-boyfriend’s apartment and discovers he's trapped in a hellish dream world, it kicks off a well-executed survival-horror trek of inventive puzzles and resource management to overcome dangerous monsters. High-production, live-action cutscenes help tell the story of a deteriorating relationship and the toll an indie horror film took on its creators, and they play an important role in gameplay. Tenebris Somnia may not look like much due to its classic pixelated presentation, but its scares and story captivate. – Our Review

Resident Evil Requiem is not just one of the best Resident Evil games, but it’s also one of the best horror games ever made. It features a unique dual-protagonist structure. Grace Ashcroft is timid, new to the whole “shooting zombies in the head while dealing with Umbrella viruses” thing, and is generally just trying to do her job. Leon S. Kennedy, however, is a veteran of all that and more. Requiem splits its runtime between the two characters, letting you experience both sides of Capcom’s marquee survival-horror style. Grace’s sections leave your hands clammy and your blood pressure high as you desperately try to survive. Leon’s sections leave your hands shaking with adrenaline and your blood pumping with excitement as he mows down zombies (sometimes literally, courtesy of those pesky chainsaws). The result is a Resident Evil game that blends two typical RE experiences – terrifying and tough or exhilarating over-the-top action – into one cohesive package. It’s perfect for someone who wants to feel scared and then soon after receive the catharsis of being the one in control, like being the tragic victim who dies in Act One of the horror movie and the last one standing who lives to tell the tale. – Our Review

Little Nightmares developer Tarsier Studios has a knack for delivering creepy side-scrolling adventures, but Reanimal eschews any whimsy to become its scariest game yet. While mechanically it is similar to Little Nightmares and still puts small children in unimaginable peril, Reanimal is capital-H horror thanks largely to its terrifying threats and disturbing animal-themed imagery (this probably isn’t the game for animal lovers; some messed-up stuff happens to these critters). Escaping the game’s island setting is thrilling and chilling whether you’re playing alone or with a friend in co-op. Months after release, we’re still thinking about Reanimal’s memorable final sequence, which is worth the price of admission on its own. – Our Review

2001’s Silent Hill 2 is considered one of the best horror video games of all time for good reason. At release, it was a graphical powerhouse, using the PlayStation 2's horsepower to create a setting that begged to be explored, even though every bone in your body said you shouldn’t. The remake from developer Bloober Team took on a big task in modernizing the game without losing the original’s soul, and it did a great job. Among all the recent Silent Hill releases (Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall), the remake is our favorite. The story of James Sunderland and his troubling relationship with his departed wife is complex, emotional, and – important for the purposes of this list – unsettling and scary. – Our Review

Alan Wake 2 is an excellent pick for some spooky madness, in the vein of David Lynch’s seminal Twin Peaks mystery-surrealist series. Don’t worry too much about the “2” part of the game’s title. You just need to know that the titular Alan Wake character is a not-great writer who acts like he’s really great, his wife is missing, and he got trapped in the ambiguous Dark Place. He’s only one half of the Alan Wake 2 equation, with his segments set in a dream-like version of New York City. Playing as him feels the most Twin Peaks-y. The other half is Saga, a police officer who arrives in the Pacific Northwest town of Bright Falls to investigate a murder that might be linked to a cult. You can expect more traditional survival-horror gameplay from her. But this is still a Remedy Entertainment game, and without spoiling anything, it goes places. And along the way, you can expect plenty of scares. Turn the lights down low (or off), light a candle, and sit back and enjoy one of Remedy’s best games. – Our Review

Square Enix has gone two-for-two with its Paranormasight series, an anthology of stories about the strange and occult. And while the more recent Mermaid's Curse is a brilliant tale all its own, the first entry – The Seven Mysteries of Honjo – brings significantly more scares. A group of people in the city of Honjo find themselves caught in a spectral battle royale, using powerful objects and conditions to curse one another, with the allure of a prize at the end. Its magic isn't just in the flowchart timeline, where you can hop between different perspectives and protagonists to see how events play out from every angle, but also in the gorgeous stereoscopic environments and narrative puzzles. Adventure games are a classic genre, and Paranormasight will remind you of what the genre is capable of the moment you slowly spin your camera around, your eyes peeking out from behind your fingers.

Survival horror can contain multitudes, and as the years have worn on, the genre has grown to encompass a wide range of action-combat mechanics. Signalis feels like a re-centering in that respect. It's an isometric survival-horror indie project from developer rose-engine, filled with clever puzzles, scarce resources, limited inventory slots, and looming, oppressive dread. As the Replika unit Elster, you delve deep into a remote complex filled with horrors and monsters, searching for something, or someone, waiting down below. While love for classic horror games and other hallmarks of genre fiction will certainly draw you in, the stylish presentation and devastatingly human core will keep you forging ahead to the finale. Once you've breached the surface of Signalis' retro-future super-structures, you won't be able to turn back.

In horror movies, audiences often groan at a protagonist for putting themselves in seemingly grave danger just to learn more about a cursed amulet or bloodthirsty killer. But in Immortality, you are the protagonist, and despite a lingering sense that you shouldn't be digging into the archives of these abandoned films, each eerie new scene makes you want to dive deeper. It's a game about Marisa Marcel, an actress who almost starred in three movies in the late 20th century, but has since disappeared. None of the movies were ever released due to mysterious circumstances, but you have access to the archived, unedited live-action footage, including behind-the-scenes conversations. By scrubbing through footage, you can select people or items in each scene and jump to random footage from any other movie that includes the same person or item. The approach to puzzle-solving is unique and keeps you appropriately disoriented. The mystery at the center is an unsettling treat to unravel, and scary in new and unexpected ways. Immortality is one of a kind and an easy recommendation for horror fans who want to try something a little different.

In the decade since launch, Dead by Daylight has continued to succeed, thanks to a dedicated (and newcomer-friendly) fanbase and its towering roster of original and licensed personas from across pop culture horror. The asymmetrical multiplayer title has become an anthology of horror’s biggest faces, including Freddy Krueger, Ghostface, Pyramid Head, and even the Xenomorph. Whether you play as a Survivor, trying to escape all manner of nightmare locations through stealth and cunning, or as a Killer, whose experience feels more like a hunting club, you’ll understand why Dead by Daylight has become a recurring destination for fans of the gruesome and bizarre.

Read about the making of Dead by Daylight and how it sunk its teeth into millions of players in our six-page exclusive feature in Issue 368 (p. 42), available in our magazine archive to anyone with a free Game Informer account.

#4386. Where To Hide Secondary Name In WoW: Forever

World of Warcraft: Forever introduces a two-part naming system, giving each character a main name and a secondary name. Rather than being unique to an individual realm, your full name must now be unique across your region.

This means you can still use a main name another player has already chosen, as long as the full two-part combination is available. But maybe you picked a random secondary name because you couldn't wait to see how your favorite starting area has changed since 2004. Luckily, you can control how that secondary name appears in-game.

Your secondary name appears above your character's head, in your character's portrait frame, and above your pet or minion. You can hide it from these UI elements if you'd prefer to see only your main name.

After unchecking the box, your secondary name will disappear from the affected displays immediately, without needing to restart the game. If you change your mind, return to the same menu and check the box again to restore it.

However, keep a couple of things in mind.

Your full character name will still appear in chat, even with the setting disabled. The setting also carries over between characters and rulesets. If you want to hide your secondary name on one character but show it on another, you'll need to change the setting each time you swap between your characters.

Pirate Software’s OnlyFangs raid controversy just got put on blast in a new WoW: Forever trailer.

In realm-based versions of World of Warcraft, players could use the same character name on different realms because names only needed to be unique within each realm. The new realmless structure removes that separation, making secondary names necessary to distinguish players who choose the same main name.

Think of secondary names like surnames. Two characters can share a main name as long as their full names differ. This flexibility is especially useful because numbers and symbols aren't supported in character names. Instead of changing the spelling of your favorite main name, you can pair it with a different secondary name. Keep in mind that Blizzard's standard naming rules still apply to both parts.

Whether you choose a meaningful surname or something random to get started, you don't have to keep it on display. Your full name remains intact, but how much of it you see is up to you.

#4385. Battlefield 6 patch finally ends the menace of the Lock-Guided Missile, shuts down the Recon Drone Sledgehammer exploit and more

Today's Battlefield 6 patch is laser-focused on taking care of some of the more infuriating bugs while also taking out a couple of exploits.

The next Battlefield 6 update is here. Having gone live just moments ago, update 1.1.1.5 is something of a midseason update, bringing a few quality of life tweaks to the game alongside some key fixes for a few of the issues that cropped up since the launch of Season 1 in late October.

This latest release is also the first to tackle some of the problems players have been running into playing Redsec battle royale, the free-to-play component that also came out recently.

Patch 1.1.1.5 is fairly limited in scope. The biggest fix in this one comes to the Lock-Guided Missiles going through flares, and generally being annoying enough to stop players from using air vehicles altogether.

The Lock-Guided Missiles were mainly used by AA vehicles, but they could also be equipped by IFVs, which made it even more of a nightmare to pilots. It got so bad that Battlefield Studios disabled it entirely while the team worked on a proper fix.

Another exploit the patch fixes is the one that allowed players to stand on the Recon Drone and reach areas they’re not supposed to. This was done by… repeatedly hitting it with a Sledgehammer. The long-running issue of vehicles not spawning for certain teams in Conquest and Breakthrough appears to have finally been fixed, too.

In terms of battle royale, the patch has a few fixes that should help make the experience more consistent, as well as improve the flow of matches. One of the more interesting addresses an issue that could eliminate the entire squad instead of reviving dead teammates when using a Mobile Spawn.

Patch 1.1.1.5 also has yet more adjustments to weapon dispersion (bloom). Some of the casses it addresses include transitioning from sprint to firing in ADS, and others where it apparently scaled with player movement speed.

#4384. Arc Raiders has proven that extraction shooters can be popular, with over 4 million copies sold in under two weeks

Arc Raiders has sold even more copies, which we should've guessed, given that the game keeps breaking its own concurrent player records.

It’s pretty clear at this stage that Arc Raiders is one of the biggest launches of 2025. More interesting than the numbers themselves, however, is that this is an extraction shooter - a subgenre which has typically been thought of as niche.

If you’ve been paying the PvPvE game any attention, you could easily see how (and why) it keeps breaking its own records.

Today, publisher Nexon announced in a press release (via Gematsu) that Arc Raiders has now sold over 4 million copies. The game came out on October 30, which means it managed to sell that many copies in a little over 10 days.

The news comes on the same day that developer Embark Studios announced that the game had more than 700,000 concurrent players across all platforms over the weekend. Over the same weekend on Steam alone, Arc Raiders broke its own Steam concurrent record with a new peak of 462,488 players - which is a significant chunk of that 700,000+ player base.

This marks the second time the extraction shooter has broken its own concurrent player records, which is something very few games have managed in the past. Arc Raiders remains a top-seller, too. On Steam, it’s currently the second-best seller globally (by revenue), sitting just below Counter-Strike 2.

“The many different ways you play and participate in ARC Raiders have completely blown us away, going far beyond what we ever imagined. You surprise us, you outsmart us, and you keep us on our toes. We wouldn’t have it any other way,” the developer wrote on Twitter.

Embark recently published a roadmap to highlight all the new content coming to the game over the remainder of this year. The first new map is set to arrive this month alongside new Arc units, new gameplay items, new events and more.

Just over the weekend, the game received several new Map Conditions that completely alter the way they play. The developer has already rolled out a couple of updates since launch, in order to tackle exploits and fix a few launchday bugs.

If you’re currently hooked on this gem of a game, we guarantee that our Arc Raiders gameplay tips will have at least one you didn’t know about. We also have more guides on how to find some of the more elusive items in the game, such as olives, lemons and apricots, and prickly pears.

#4383. Arc Raiders' new map will be unlocked through a community event that starts today, and everyone has to donate

It looks like it's going to take the Arc Raiders community a bit of work to unlock the game's next map.

As many of Arc Raiders’ regular players predicted, the game’s first post-launch map won’t just be available for everyone, it will instead be closely tied to a community event. Breaking New Ground is the name of that event, and it’s one where everyone will need to contribute in order to rebuild some old tunnels and unlock the way to Stella Montis.

The event kicks off today alongside the release of the game’s latest patch. The ask is relatively simple: players must commit Basic Materials to the project so that the tunnels can be rebuilt. This option will be available to anyone who’s played at least five rounds.

If you’ve spent any time in Arc Raiders, you’ll know that Basic Materials are things like Metal parts, Fabric, Chemicals, Rubber Parts, and Plastic Parts - most of which are easy to find in the game’s various maps.

Even beyond the ultimate goal of unlocking the new map, donations will also reward you with Merits, which is a new event currency, though there’s a cap on how many you can earn.

Once enough materials have been collected, the next phase of the event, Staking Our Claim, will begin, which will bring a new progression track to the game, and make Stella Montis available for players to visit.

Developer Embark describes the new environment as unlike any that we have seen in the game so far. It’s a facility carved into the northern mountains, which means it’s going to have a near-pristine look; quite the contrast with the rest of the game’s environments.

Stella Montis also has its own Arc enemies, loot, schematics, and other gameplay items. You can look forward to coming across the Shredder, a close-quarter Arc unit exclusive to the new map for now.

Then there’s The Matriarch, a somehow even larger version of the Queen. Thankfully, it will only be available under a specific map condition, so you’re in no danger of running into her randomly. The update will also introduce a new legendary weapon, two new grenades, and three new mines.

Staking Our Claim will only run until December, which is when the next stage of the game’s roadmap will kick off. Then, the Cold Snap update will introduce the Flickering Flames event, the first snowfall Map Condition, and the Expedition Project voluntary wipe.

In case you’re still missing them, here’s how to find lemons and apricots, prickly pear, and olives.

#4382. Zenless Zone Zero's new Krampus squad know when you've been bad or good in a Christmas-y update to close out 2025

Zenless Zone Zero's 2.4 update is a chunky one, adding a new faction to the action RPG's roster alongside a new area, and fresh playable characters.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program was a big one, bringing us all the news about Version 2.4, the next major update. It’s called On the Precipice of the Abyss, and it will be available to download on November 26.

On the Precipice of the Abyss has tendrils in many areas of the game, touching several parts of its fiction as well as gameplay, so it’s one to watch out for.

Version 2.4’s biggest claim to fame is the introduction of the Krampus Compliance Authority, a new faction that’s affiliated with TOPS. This looks to be the oversight committee, dispatched after the squad’s adventure beneath Timesworn Hill.

The events of this narrative arch follow on from the Timesworn Hill crisis, which is partly why we’re going to a new area as part of this update. The old mining site can now be explored for the first time in a decade, now that the Miasma has begun to recede.

Our newcomers this time around are Dialyn and Banyue. Dialyn is an S-Rank Physical Stun Agent who’s a former customer service specialist. This isn’t just a backstory, however, as it plays into her gameplay.

Dialyn relies on two resources: Customer Complaint and Positive Review, but her core role is to stun enemies and allow teammates to unleash their Ults, with a nice boost to boot.

Banyue is another S-Rank, though he’s a Fire Rupture Agent. He uses his martial arts expertise to create combinations of might and grandeur. In combat, he pulls from Adrenaline and Wrathful Fires, alternating between the two to fuel his actions. There’s a bit of rhythm to his gameplay that might take you a little while to master.

Even more characters will join as part of this update, in the form of not one but two new Bangboo units. Birkblick is Krampus' own proprietary lil bunny fella, who brings a sensor array that can transform into a cannon in combat, essentially tracking and immediately nuking targets. Then there’s Bild N. Boolok, a Support Agent-affiliated Physical damage dealing Bangboo bringing a giant block hammer to the fight to, well, smash enemies with.

It’s a bit of a winter party in Version 2.4, it seems, as the update will bring back Hugo (Attack - Ice), and Ellen (Attack - Ice), too.

You can also look forward to the return of the Bangboo auto chess event, which now includes PvE stages with unique rewards. In fact, playing this event is how you could get Bild N. Boolok for free. Lightstream Notes is another event that will be available for the duration of this update, and it will let you tag along with Ye Shunguang to New Eridu.
