#4251. No Disc, No Buy and PS5 Blackout Protests Fail to Impact PlayStation

Active users increases, digital sales percentage increases

Sony has published its financial report for the Q2 period of fiscal year 2026, the stretch of time in which some PS5 fans took a stand against PlayStation decisions of recent years to make their frustrations heard.

After years of proposed disappointment surrounding Sony's first-party game output, studio closures, and a shift into the live service, everything came to a head over PlayStation's decision to stop manufacturing physical versions of new titles from January 2028 onwards.

Fans and organisations set up protests to try and make their voices heard, such as the No Disc, No Buy slogan, and most famously, the PS5 blackout rally by Does It Play. The latter encouraged fans to turn their PS5 consoles off for a week to try and hit Sony where it hurts: its financial results, most notably where Sony reports its monthly active users per quarter.

Those numbers have now been made public, and they confirm the protests haven't affected Sony's results.

For the Q2 period in which the protests took place, Sony recorded 127 million monthly active users. This is eight million more users than it had last year during the same period, and an increase of two million over the first quarter of 2026.

There was a 7% increase in monthly active users for September compared to the same month in the last fiscal year, which resulted in a record high for September. Total playtime for the entire quarter increased by 4% year-on-year, as Sony sees its engagement on PlayStation "steadily improving".

On the other hand, the No Disc, No Buy campaign is designed to tell Sony that if a game isn't shipped on a physical disc, then that person won't buy it. During this period, 78% of all "full game software" purchases were for the digital version. That's purely "full game" purchases; the percentage doesn't include DLC or microtransactions.

That's a 6% increase compared to the same period of time last year.

Customer spending across physical and digital software is actually on the up for both types of media, but digital continues to dwarf physical. Sony made ¥43.1 billion in the Q2 quarter of this fiscal year from physical games, which is almost ¥8 billion more than the same period last year.

However, digital games brought in ¥330.8 billion. That's an increase of ¥60.5 billion compared to the Q2 period of fiscal year 2025.

It was always up for debate how much of an impact these kinds of campaigns could really have. It's likely Sony was aware they were taking place, but if they make no tangible impact, then it's something the company can very easily sweep under the rug. It also came out that nearly half of the social media accounts pushing the No Disc, No Buy campaign may have been fake bots.

PlayStation has never commented on the fan protests, and it hasn't shared any updates or changes to its plans to stop physical disc production from the start of 2028. With this evidence now to hand, it probably sees fit to continue with what it's doing.

In the same time period those fan protests took place, the monthly active user count and the digital-to-physical software sales ratio both increased. How do you react to the news? Post your thoughts in the comments below.

@Ganon821 Yes, that’s what is part of this that for some reason many people don’t understand, it’s a form of selection bias. The numbers aren’t measuring exactly what they think it’s measuring. If there’s no product (or limited product) to buy, then of course sales go down: but it doesn’t mean people don’t want to buy the thing that’s not available! 😂 I still frequent brick and mortar stores looking for games on disc and I gradually can’t find anything I want. I used to walk out of GameStop with 1-2 games nearly every time I went there, and now I go and see very limited stock of games. So of course I don’t buy anything. I then go on the PSN store and buy a digital game instead, despite my preferences. To show this data and imply there is waning interest in buying physical is somewhat deceptive. It’s confirmation bias to see the numbers continue to trend toward digital when it’s the only option. There’s another logical fallacy called “Hobson’s Choice” going on too — which is “the illusion of choice”, or the “take it or leave it” mandate, so if you “take it” then those less educated would say “see… you chose it!” when in reality, there was no real choice at all.

There’s also some confounding variables going on in the data interpretation. But I’ll try to refrain from continuing to upset the digital crowd with logic. 😜

And to be clear, I’m not saying that the move to digital isn’t real and inevitable, but I do find all these numbers supposedly supporting the fact “no one wants physical” to be grossly misrepresented.

@atthegates I'm afraid you don't understand why consoles are always cheaper than PCs.

Firstly, they're machines architected from the outset to be good at one thing only: living-room gaming. Sony can afford to invest millions in R&D to design custom components, and arrange them in a hyper optimized way. The same goes for the OS and SDK.

So, in a like-for-like scenario, a game will usually perform better on a console when compared to an equivalent PC.

But it doesn't stop there. Economies of scale also play a massive role in guaranteeing consoles are cheaper. Sony sources components in bulk, by the millions, and naturally gets a lower price.

And finally, Sony doesn't need to make a profit on console sales, because the lion's share of PlayStation's revenue comes from the content and services line (games, PS+). Yes, the subsidization days may be behind us, but not making a profit is enough to guarantee PCs will always be substantially pricier. The Steam Machine is an emblematic example.

It's pretty basic business logic, and it all points to the gap in prices between consoles and PCs to only get larger.

#4250. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4249. Nintendo Reiterates Plans For Zelda's 40th Anniversary

"We will pursue a variety of initiatives"

You can't really avoid it in the gaming space right now, but if you did somehow miss it, Nintendo is currently celebrating the 40th anniversary of the Zelda series.

Following the release of Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2 this week, the firm has now issued a reminder about the series' anniversary in its latest financial results briefing. For the remainder of this year and throughout next year, it will pursue a "variety of initiatives" to celebrate the series.

It's not only focused on game releases, and fans who cherish the "earlier titles", but also merchandise, music (a worldwide concert), and of course, the Zelda movie - scheduled to arrive early next year. Here's what's on the way:

"Over the course of this year and next, we will pursue a variety of initiatives to celebrate the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda. In addition to games, we will expand opportunities for consumers to experience its world through the movie, music, character merchandise, and more.

"We will make the series even more appealing by offering different ways to enjoy it, both for those who cherish its earlier titles and for those discovering it for the first time."

You can get a recap about all the recent Zelda 40th anniversary announcements in our round up of the Zelda Direct:

Guide Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct - Every Announcement And Trailer

What else would you like to see from the Zelda 40th anniversary celebrations? Got any game requests? Tell us in the comments.

Liam is a news writer and reviewer on Nintendo Life. He's been writing about games for more than 15 years and is a lifelong fan of many iconic video game characters.

#4248. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#4247. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

Exclusive: The Rings of Power season 3 might be the darkest season yet of the Lord of the Rings prequel

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Rings of Power season 3 begins at the darkest moment yet for Middle-earth. Sauron is in possession of the Nine Rings for men and is plotting his path to forge the One Ring, all the while sending his Orcs out to conquer new locales.

As a result, the stakes are pretty high for each of the show's beloved characters, and the showrunners reveal that there will be "tragic consequences".

"The elves are clinging on to being able to hold Sauron at bay, but only by the power of their three rings," co-showrunner J.D. Payne tells GamesRadar+. "And Sauron, his plan this season is to be able to neutralize the power of those rings by making One Ring to rule them all. Beyond that, he's also recruiting a massive army by giving out the Nine Rings for men."

As Patrick McKay adds, it's a tense situation to be in and one they wanted to acknowledge with real stakes. "In Lord of the Rings, people turn to the dark side; they fall to evil, and when that happens, there are tragic consequences," he adds. "And we felt that it was important for the audience to feel those viscerally, and for people that you love and whose stories you're excited to watch continue, sometimes the end is not happy for them. That can be painful. But it should be. It shouldn't be fun."

As Payne alludes to, the main frontier against Sauron is the Elves, led by a war-beaten Gil-galad, played by Benjamin Walker. He tells GamesRadar+ that it's not looking great for them when the third season kicks off, either. "It's the little Dutch boy with his finger in the dam, kind of going, 'Everything's fine!' Everything is not fine. If I take my finger out, we're all going to drown. Yeah, it's not great. Outlook is bleak, and the tool, the weapon we have been using are the rings, the power of it is eroding and becoming potentially ominous. So we're in a position where we can't do this on our own."

They look to Númenór, which is facing its own problems of civil war, with Míriel and Pharazôn split across two sides of the conflict. While they're out of the battle with Sauron for now, darkness is on the horizon for the kingdom too, as Míriel star Cynthia Addai-Robinson alludes to.

"There's going to be a lot of heartbreak in this particular part of the world," she explains. "And obviously there is a sense of being duty-bound, there is a sense of sacrifice for the greater good, and they are all driven by this particular worldview, and it just so happens that on the other side of that is Pharazôn and sort of what Númenor has become under his leadership and trying to make sure that it doesn't get to the point of no return. So I might be biased, but I love the Númenor storyline this season, and I think it's doing a very good job of taking us toward the inevitable, if you know where it all goes."

The expanding darkness is felt in all corners of Middle-earth too, as the Dwarven kingdom of Khazad-dûm has shut its doors to try and protect the Dwarven rings. Durin star Owain Arthur explains: "The stakes just keep on getting higher and higher. This is it, and the more power Sauron gets, the more danger there is, the more doom and gloom there is in Middle-earth, but there's hope."

The showrunners were keen to find some levity in this darkness too. This mainly comes from the romantic storyline between Galadriel and her long-lost husband Celeborn, played by franchise newcomer Jamie Campbell Bower. Their reunion is a point of light, which J.D. Payne says was one of their "main objectives this season".

"Romance was an important thing for us this season, and we brought in some writers in our writers' room. We asked specifically, we said, 'We want you to be really hard on us, be really hard on the story, and how do we make this romance work,'" Payne says. "You know, we looked at things that you know in sort of our shared canon of The Princess Bride and Before Sunset, that you know we both love, and you know these stories of what happens when people who loved each other once and have been separated for a long time get back together again. How do you pick the relationship back up?"

The answers will all be revealed when The Rings of Power season 3 begins on Prime Video on November 11. For more on Middle-earth, check out our guide on how to watch the Lord of the Rings movies in order.

#4245. Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

Finally, a PC specification list that actually indicates resolution and framerate targets, and doesn't leave console players behind.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

#4244. Review: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 - The First COD I've Cared About In Ages

For many years now, I've felt like I knew exactly what to expect from a new Call of Duty game without ever needing to play it. When I do eventually get stuck in, because I'm a COD enjoyer deep down, they're usually par for the course: action-packed, testosterone-fuelled kiddie crack designed to overstimulate, lock you in, and keep you playing.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 surprised me, though. Activision's latest entry is so much more than my rather crass judgement would’ve suggested, delivering the best campaign experience I've had with the FPS series since World At War. What a corker this one is, let me tell you!

So, let's talk campaign. It's easily the most cinematic, well-acted and tense narrative to come out of Call of Duty in years. Whilst it's fun to swing Captain Price's big, meaty fists around, for me, the real stars are the Korean and American marines who make up Sierra-1.

Throughout the 6-8 hours it takes to complete, MW4's globetrotting campaign pops us into the boots of Private First Class Park Hyun-Jun and wastes no time unleashing a full-scale invasion upon South Korea. As far as opening missions go, 'Mayhem Walking' is jaw-dropping in its depiction of the devastation of Hajin City. It’s an absolute banger.

Defending against North Korean paratroopers sets the tone perfectly for a campaign that just doesn't falter. Mission after mission impressed me and kept me wanting more. I suppose my assumptions were still at least half-correct.

Yes, it's a thrill to experience Price face off against his former teammate Ghost in exhilarating knife-to-knife combat. It's nerve-wracking to ransack North Korean homes in search of defectors. It's just that I've never doubted Call of Duty's knack for pulling off an action-packed spectacle: rather, its ability to make me care about the characters caught up in it that I’ve questioned.

Sierra-1, along with the few stragglers who link up with the squad, provides that human element and gives me a reason to care about the people I’m fighting alongside. Military conscription is mandatory across Korea, and as a result, MW4's characters are far more relatable and genuine, adding a sense of personal investment in their survival that I hadn't experienced before.

Then, once I'd shot all the bad dudes who needed shooting and overthrown the biggest bad dude, Modern Warfare 4's latest iteration of DMZ was there to keep me locked in. It's clever, really. With the campaign being my favourite part of the package, DMZ taps into that by carrying the narrative forward through its PvPvE extraction mode.

I've never considered myself a big fan of the looting and extraction gameplay loop, with Marathon being my main exception. Sure, it's thrilling when you get it right, but it's even more frustrating when you get it wrong. I get what I'm talking about is predominantly a skill issue, but for a casual 'coddy' like me, I think Activision may have got it right.

Deploying into the DMZ with a friend and working through its various story missions has been a lot of fun. One of the earlier missions particularly tickled me, as I was tasked with extracting a bedbound patient from a hospital.

I don't know about you, but I found it quite silly - in the best possible way - to duck enemy fire behind a hospital gurney occupied by a sedated chap. Wheeling him through the facility, up elevators, and away in a chopper was a lot of fun. Even if realism should probably have demanded that he extract in the form of Swiss cheese.

There's a lot to DMZ that I'd wager I haven't fully experienced yet, but I reckon I've sampled enough of its ingredients to appreciate what makes the extraction mode such a tasty side dish to the campaign. The skill trees feel a little forced, but upgrading my chosen operators is moreish, and taking out baddies to warrant a death squad coming after you is thrilling.

So far, I haven't encountered any immediate PvP deaths that have made me want to curl up and never deploy into the DMZ again. Overall, it's decent, but there’s one thing I honestly wish wasn't in the game (campaign included): the developer's decision to repeatedly put dogs in the firing line.

John Wick was years ago. If the intention is to motivate players by shooting dogs, consider this my objection. I don’t think it’s a necessary storytelling device, and I’d happily see it left out in the future. Just let sleeping dogs lie.

Another minor issue I have with Modern Warfare 4 falls under its multiplayer offering. Specifically, skill-based matchmaking and some inconsistencies with hit registration.

I actually really like the gunplay and movement in MW4 (my favourite being MW2), but thank f*** omnimovement is gone. Everyone seems to move more like actual humans and less like over-caffeinated gibbons. The gameplay itself, across all modes, is a lot of fun and feels great. It's just that my competition always seems to be that little bit better than me.

Listen, I'm not claiming to be anything special when it comes to Call of Duty PvP, but I'm not crap either. I just don't have time to master movement, equipment and loadouts. Going in raw, I'd still say I'm pretty handy at pointing and shooting, which usually leads to me being placed against decent opposition. My problem with COD multiplayer, and I've felt this way for years, is that you either lean forward, join the sweats and have a less enjoyable time, or they destroy you, which isn't much fun either. Modern Warfare 4 feels like it hasn't fully figured out that balance either.

Don't get me wrong, competition is great, and I do love getting spicy from time to time. But when you're 34 and hopping on for one or two games after suffering through a long day of AI fearmongering, can't a guy just sit down and have fun?

It's made worse by the fact that, even when I do slap up, I still lose fights because of inconsistent hit registration. In MW4, I've landed five registered shots from my 25th Anniversary Xbox M4 rifle square into an enemy's face, only to get folded by a single shot to the gut. It hurts.

The bones are there with multiplayer, but the system needs some work.

As an overall package, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is generally solid. It looks and plays great on Xbox Series X, delivering its cinematic campaign and a thoughtful iteration of DMZ, all complemented by the fun-junky action of multiplayer.

This is the first COD game I've really cared about since World at War, and I can actually see myself playing it for quite a while.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is a certified banger and thoroughly deserving of all the praise heaped upon it. This is the first COD game I've genuinely cared about in over a decade, and it’s one of 2026's best new titles.

Its cinematic action, star-studded cast, and tense depiction of Korea at war deliver an unforgettable batch of campaign missions. Once it's all over, DMZ impresses with a surprising level of depth and plenty of opportunity for co-op shenanigans. Multiplayer is exactly what you'd expect: moreish fun for hours on end, but suffers the familiar curse of SBMM.

If only the devs could ditch the frequent and forced killing of in-game dogs, then I'd easily give MW4 a higher score.

Review copy provided by ActivisionHow we review productsScoring Policy

Craig is a Staff Writer and former Video Producer at Pure Xbox, where he covers the biggest games in the world of Xbox.

#4243. Nintendo Highlights Multiple Major Third-Party Releases On The Way To Switch 2 In 2027

The third-party support for the Switch 2 has been mostly outstanding so far, with releases such as Cyberpunk 2077 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

It doesn't seem to be slowing down, either. In its latest financial results briefing, Nintendo has now shared a reminder about some of the titles coming to the system over the next year. This includes games like Final Fantasy VII Revelation and FromSoft's Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods, which was recently delayed.

Here are Nintendo's highlights. Layton's new outing and a few other titles also get a shoutout, as late 2026 arrivals.

"More third-party multiplatform titles coming to Nintendo on day one, in addition to titles developed for Nintendo Switch 2"

Nintendo has also used this opportunity to share some charts, illustrating how third-party continues to provide support for overall software sales on the Switch and Switch 2. It also plays a major role in driving engagement.

"Ongoing sales of our previously released evergreen titles, together with sales of third-party titles, provide substantial support for overall software unit sales.

"...Titles from software publishers account for a significant share of software unit sales, making a substantial contribution to our business. Furthermore, their software has a strong presence among download-only titles, which are not included in this graph, and plays a major role in sustaining engagement with our hardware."

On the first-party front, Nintendo has this week reconfirmed the release windows for multiple upcoming Switch 2 titles. You can find out what else is on the way in our previous story.

#4242. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4241. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4240. PS5 Closing in on 100 Million Sales as Gradual Drop-Off Continues

That's another 2.6 million PS5 consoles sold

Sony sold another 2.6 million PS5 consoles during the second quarter of its 2026 fiscal year, bringing the total number of systems sold to 97.9 million.

It should surpass the 100 million sales milestone by the end of the next fiscal report, but the downward trend in sales has continued. PlayStation sold four million PS5 machines during the same quarter of its last fiscal year, confirming 1.4 million fewer systems were sold in the quarter just gone.

The Q1 period of fiscal year 2026 also recorded a reduced number of PS5 consoles sold: 1.6 million compared to 2.5 million in the previous fiscal year.

Besides the gradual decrease in PS5 system sales, though, practically all of PlayStation's results for the quarter are on the up.

It sold 88.2 million PS5 and PS4 games, which is an increase of 7.9 million over the same time period last fiscal year. 8.2 million of those sales were first-party projects, which is 1.9 million more purchases than the same quarter in the previous fiscal year.

Once it hits the 100 million sales milestone, the PS5 will be the fourth PlayStation console to manage the feat, with PS1, PS2, and PS4 all managing the accomplishment. The PS3 topped out at around 87.4 million units sold.

News No Disc, No Buy and PS5 Blackout Protests Fail to Impact PlayStation

Active users increases, digital sales percentage increases

With perhaps the most anticipated entertainment release of all time right around the corner in GTA 6, it'll be interesting to see how much of an impact it has on PS5 console sales. The upcoming Rockstar release could cause a huge boost in system sales, though Sony needs the stock in place to facilitate that.

The Q3 quarter is typically the time when Sony sees its most console sales, as evidenced by Q3 in fiscal year 2025, when it sold 7.9 million PS5 systems. Despite the downward trend in sales as the current generation reaches its end, could GTA 6 provide the boost to PS5 to sell more than last year? We'll have to wait and see.

#4239. Matt Damon says not sleeping for days on The Odyssey worked in his favour: "[Odysseus] probably didn’t sleep last night"

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

Matt Damon accidentally went full method while filming The Odyssey and didn't sleep for days, just like his Greek warrior

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It turns out that it wasn't all makeup and that Matt Damon really was just that exhausted in The Odyssey, as the star reveals he was awake for almost two days straight while filming the movie's most intense scene.

"I had it happen two or three times on this movie where I just didn’t sleep," explains Damon in an interview with GQ. "I was tired and I went to bed, and I’m sure everyone’s had that feeling where you’ve got to get up the next day and you have something that you have to do and you can’t fall asleep and you’re kicking the blanket around and you’re staring at the ceiling. By the time I got to work to do the scene with Samantha [Morton], I hadn’t slept in 24 hours, and by the end of the day it was 36 or whatever."

We assume that Damon is talking about that unforgettable scene in Circe's cabin. After losing many soldiers to the giants of Telepylos, Odysseus' men begin to lose trust in him, so when they reach Circe's island, they split up. But when they stumble upon Circe's hut, she lures them with a magical broth and eventually turns them into squealing pigs. Odysseus goes looking for them and confronts the witch, and in a long and tense conversation, we learn about Circe's dark past and twisted motivations.

Damon says his sleep deprivation actually helped him in this scene, which makes sense, as Odysseus himself wouldn't be that well-rested either after watching his men be torn apart by Laestrygonians and then desperately searching for a new island to dock at before he and his men starve to death. "I remember thinking the great thing about this character is he probably didn’t sleep last night," added Damon. "So the weariness was very real for a lot of the movie."

The whole project was a huge undertaking, though. The Odyssey was shot on location around the world, from remote caves in Greece to open scenes, where Christoper Nolan got through 400 miles of film while shooting on the open sea. But Damon says he is glad he got to do it at this point in his career, adding, "I don’t think I would’ve appreciated it as much 20 years ago," as even though "there was a lot of physical discomfort that was temporary," he "felt so grateful to be there. I was just so joyful the whole time that I didn’t really notice any of that."

For more, check out our ranking of the best Christopher Nolan movies and keep up with all of the new movies heading your way.

#4238. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4237. The Best-Rated Game Of 2026 Has Just Changed, But Xbox Still Has Two Titles In The Top 10

The news cycle has undoubtedly been dominated with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake today, and for good reason - it's become the best-rated game of 2026 according to Metacritic with a whopping 96 average rating.

That means the top 10 has some shuffling to do, but even with Zelda taking top spot (and even if GTA 6 surpasses it in November), there are still two Xbox first-party releases that are almost certainly locked into the top 10 for 2026.

The first of these is Forza Horizon 6, which now sits in seventh position across all platforms with its 90 average rating, serving as the best full game that Xbox has released this year according to Metacritic.

The other is DOOM: The Dark Ages - Revelations, which might be an expansion to an existing title, but is still counted by the platform (and to be fair, basically serves as an extra game anyway) and sits in sixth place with a 91 rating.

Go down a bit further, and Gears of War: E-Day is the next highest-rated Xbox first-party game with an average rating of 87, followed by Modern Warfare 4 at 85, Diablo IV: Lord of Hatred at 84 and Halo: Campaign Evolved at 81.

In a nutshell, it's been a pretty incredible year for video games! Don't forget that Sektori, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered and Mina The Hollower have all released on Xbox this year as well, while Xbox still has another massive first-party title dropping tomorrow in the form of World of Warcraft: Forever - albeit only on PC.

So, what do you reckon to this list? Are you getting the new Zelda this week? Tell us down below.

#4236. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4235. Nintendo To Continue Delivering Movies Beyond Live-Action Zelda, Unsurprisingly

Nintendo is now fully committed to the movie business thanks to Super Mario and the upcoming live-action Zelda film, due out 30th April 2027.

During the latest financial briefing, company president Shuntaro Furukawa has reiterated how the Japanese firm intends to "continue delivering movies" with its partners beyond the Zelda film - while also reassuring fans that each film will be "carefully" crafted.

The plan is to also establish a "framework", allowing for ongoing production. Here's the graphic attached to these comments:

"As announced, a live-action movie of The Legend of Zelda is scheduled for release in 2027, and we plan to continue delivering movies in the years that follow.

"We will work with our partners to carefully craft each film, while establishing a framework that supports ongoing production."

The Galaxy Movie has already provided enough evidence of another Mario movie, but Nintendo hasn't officially said anything.

There have also been some rumours about the Zelda movie going beyond a single film, but the first one still needs to come out (and make bank at the global box office).

Furukawa has also issued a reminder about how the combined worldwide box office sales of the animated Mario Movies have now exceeded two billion US dollars, further expanding Nintendo's reach to new audiences and regions.

"We believe these movies have provided an opportunity for people to get to know Mario, including people in regions where our dedicated video game platform business has had limited reach and people who do not normally play games."

#4234. After rumors of a delay, Disney confirms Avengers: Secret Wars release date

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Secret Wars isn't going anywhere (for now)

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Despite some well-meaning discussion around whether Avengers: Secret Wars would make its release date, it appears Disney and Marvel Studios have no intention of a delay.

As documented by Hablemos de Cine, the Argentinian Disney 2027 Upfront event featured confirmation that – for now, at least – Secret Wars remains set for December 17, 2027. The 2028 movies, X-Men, Ghost Rider, and Black Panther 3, are also still locked in.

A direct sequel to Avengers: Doomsday, Secret Wars is set to bring the Multiverse Saga to a close. As of right now, the only confirmed details we have arrived courtesy of San Diego Comic-Con in 2024 – namely, Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom would be joined by the main casts of Thunderbolts and Fantastic Four.

Anthony Mackie also said he will be back as Captain America, but has said he won't be filming Secret Wars until July – hence the whispers that Secret Wars would need to be pushed back into 2028 to accommodate various actors' schedules.

As of late July this year, directors Anthony and Joe Russo were starting to "sweat" with how close they were to beginning Secret Wars filming but, unless everything has been completely under wraps, it appears there hasn't been a great deal of progress made with production this year.

Still, there's the small matter of Avengers: Doomsday to get out the way first. A new synopsis promises an "existential threat" amid the uncertain future of the multiverse.

Early ticket sales are reflective of the excitement around the movie, too, with numbers already crossing $125 million over a month out from release. Maybe Secret Wars can wait a little longer?

For more an all things MCU, we have complete guides on upcoming Marvel movies and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#4233. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or plan to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

#4232. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4231. PS5 Exclusive Marvel's Wolverine Off to a Soft Start, 2.4 Million Copies Sold to Date

Sony has officially confirmed sales figures for Marvel's Wolverine for the first time, as part of its recent financial update.

According to the report, the PS5 exclusive superhero action adventure has sold 2.4 million units as of 4th November, 2026.

The game launched on 15th September, so this sales figure is its performance after 50 days on the market.

While it may initially sound reasonably strong, it doesn't make for flattering comparisons with other titles.

For example, Marvel's Spider-Man 2 sold 2.5 million copies in its first 24 hours, and reached 5 million in 11 days.

Last year's Ghost of Yotei, meanwhile, reached 3.3 million sales in its first month.

With Marvel's Wolverine reportedly costing around $300 million to produce, it's seemingly still got some way to go before it's a profitable product.

Previous sales estimates from a couple of analytical firms have been proven fairly accurate, then, but it's always good to get proper, confirmed numbers from Sony itself.

While this sales figure means a fairly slow start for a game of this scope and budget, it's worth remembering that Marvel's Wolverine was the USA's top-selling game of September in full game dollar sales. It was also the best launch month for a Sony game since Helldivers 2.

Having said that, its early momentum doesn't appear to have carried through to October; in last month's PS Store charts, the game dropped to 14th in the US and isn't in Europe's top 20 at all.

So, it's been a success in some ways, but there's still some ground to make up. In a sense, Insomniac's Spider-Man series picks up the slack, having sold around 60 million units total, so I doubt Wolverine's somewhat soft sales performance will be too big a concern for the higher-ups.

Mixed news for this title, then, but overall I think it'll be fine — the game will slowly rack up more sales over time, and it's about to have its first holiday season, where there will no doubt be a spike.

Keanu Reeves is officially back as John Wick

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Keanu Reeves will officially return as John Wick in an animated prequel film about his infamous Impossible Task.

In the films, it's revealed that Wick pulled off this impossible task in order to win his freedom from the High Table and retire for love. Of course, his wife, Helen, then dies from an illness, leaving behind a gift of a puppy… and you know the rest.

Per Variety, Reeves has closed a deal to return in the film, which will see him on a mission to kill all of his rivals in a single night. Ultraman: Rising director Shannon Tindle will helm the film, with Ryan and Kaz Firpo penning the script. Chad Stahelski, Basil Iwanyk, Erica Lee, and Reeves will produce.

While Reeves is back in animation, then, it seems he'll also be back in live-action, too. Wick died at the end of John Wick 4, but returned for a supporting role in the prequel movie Ballerina, starring Ana de Armas. He'll also be returning for John Wick 5, despite being dead.

"Keanu, Chad [Stahelski], Basil [Iwanyk] and Erica [Lee] would not return unless they had something truly phenomenal and fresh to say with these characters and this world," Lionsgate's motion picture chairman Adam Fogelson said at CinemaCon. Iwanyk and Lee added: "It's so important to get this story right and give John's story the proper next step. It's exciting to take the first step on that road."

Time will tell what John Wick 5 involves, but for now, we can look forward to seeing Reeves back in animation.

#4229. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4228. Xbox Announces Two New Methods To Play Games Through The Cloud

"Starting today, we’re rolling out two previews for XBOX Cloud Gaming."

Team Xbox continues to make improvements to playing games through the cloud, and they've just announced two new methods for doing just that - both launching in "preview" form later today.

The first of these is the ability to use your phone as a controller, which will be available across Android and iOS on supported Smart TVs (including certain Amazon, LG, Samsung and other models) in this preview.

To access this, you'll just need to turn on the "Preview Features" in the Xbox app on your supported TV:

To try it, turn on Preview Features under Settings > Account in the latest supported Smart TV experience. When you launch a game without a physical controller connected, you’ll see an option to use your phone for that session.

The second new method is something called "cloud connect", which allows you to connect using Wi-Fi to reduce input latency in Xbox Cloud Gaming titles. The catch here is that it only works with the new Xbox Nano Controller for now, and even then it "won’t work with every cloud gaming experience yet" during the preview phase.

Here's a bit more about it, along with an image:

Players in the U.S. can preview cloud connect with the XBOX Nano Controller starting today. Instead of a Bluetooth connection to your TV, cloud connect uses your Wi-Fi to connect directly to the cloud server running your game. That can help reduce input latency, so gameplay may feel more responsive. Cloud connect is still an early test, so it won’t work with every cloud gaming experience yet. For now, you can try it on supported Smart TVs and the web.

For what it's worth, it's been rumoured by Windows Central that the "cloud connect" feature will become part of all Xbox controllers in the future, but for the time being it remains exclusive to the Nano.

So, there you go! It seems these will remain in a preview state for a decent amount of time as the team aims to "shape the experience", so be sure to provide feedback if you have any improvements in mind.

We'll leave you with a related story about the new Nano controller that released today down below.

#4227. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

#4226. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

Now that the $55 billion deal seeing EA go private under Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners is done and dusted, the former two are reportedly looking to purchase another big name in gaming: Unity.

The EA buyout hasn't been a simple process, to say the least, with the studio facing backlash following the closure of BioWare and cancellation of Mass Effect 5, but it's settled – legally, anyway – nonetheless. As for Unity, news of its own potential move under the PIF and Silver Lake's wing comes directly from Reuters, which claims to learn as much from anonymous "people familiar with the matter." So, what exactly is happening?

Well, according to the report, Unity – also operating as Unity Software Inc. and Unity Technologies or simply Unity – is in talks regarding its acquisition, with Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia's PIF at the forefront. If you're out of the loop on what Unity itself is, it's most well-known for its cross-platform game engine, which powers quite a few notable titles, both AAA and indie. Think everything from Genshin Impact to Among Us.

As for the possible deal, it's important to note that Silver Lake already owns about 8% of Unity. And, as per Reuters, it recently approached the company alongside the PIF in, discussing a valuation of some $25 billion. The parties involved haven't struck any sort of solid deal yet, however, with Unity supposedly working with an investment bank to see all of its options before anything concrete occurs.

It's difficult to tell just what will happen at this point, but I'm certain this will spur a good bit of discussion among developers and users alike. For instance, what could this buyout mean for Unity, should it happen? That remains to be seen – and, sadly, neither Unity, Silver Lake, nor the PIF responded to Reuters' requests for comment, so this is all we're working with in terms of public knowledge about the deal… should it be underway, that is.

"Asking the AI to reproduce a game that has already been made does not make you Kojima," says Unity CEO launching an AI you can use to reproduce games.

#4224. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.
